content.text: Related to this error:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2486
Algorithm for this:
for each rdf resource get the graph
find all the triples whose objects begin with the repository base
do a head on each one of those resources and if it is a binary resource, filter the triple in question from the graph
An initial attempt:
https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/16c46a8c8480738081aa503c5f313e8ad514bf2c

The graph comparison is still failing when binaries are not included in the export, even though the original and destination graphs show the same number of triples.  So the correct triples seem to be getting filtered, but nevertheless there are difference showing up in the resulting graphs.
Waiting on this issue to determine next steps:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2515
For Python's rdflib, the relevant issues are described here:
https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/wiki/Literal-reworking

It appears that the triples should be compared using the node.eq method rather than == to have the comparison based on the abstract RDF syntax rather than a lexical comparison of the representation in turtle.

Creating a PR that works with the changes to the import/export tool in FCREPO-2515.  It also includes a method for doing a more relaxed comparison of untyped literals when differences in graphs are noticed.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/pull/48
: when you have a chance, can you review this?
Resolved by
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/32bd8de046a4c7566037ce3d08e6eba091c1efb0
When importing/exporting RDF only, the verification tool needs to filter triples that refer to the binaries from the original graph, in order to avoid false mismatches.
